note: Chapter 2 dialogue, Paper and Iron (Port Linden, Thornwood). id, speaker, line, emotion (neutral/dry/warm/angry/afraid/tired/amused/sad/tense). Speaker voice fields name voice types from voices.json. Original writing.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Brick, coal smoke and a steamboat whistle. Greer says Eben Shale wears a necktie here. I'd pay to see the knot.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: That's not a printing press running. That's one being argued with.

lines.speaker: ebbing
lines.line: The man said the press, Wade. Not the furniture. He's particular about furniture.

lines.speaker: snell
lines.line: Then he can come swing the hammer himself. Two dollars don't cover lifting.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: That is a Washington hand press, gentlemen. It is older than either of you and considerably better read.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Morning. Is this the newspaper, or did I walk in on a review?

lines.speaker: ebbing
lines.line: Paper's closed, ma'am. Shut for repairs. Come back in a month. Or don't, that's simpler.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Two dollars, I heard. That's wages for breaking a press. Nobody's paying you for a funeral, and I'd hate to see you work for free.

lines.speaker: snell
lines.line: She's got a point, Carl. She's got two, and they're both looking at us.

lines.speaker: ebbing
lines.line: You tell the man it was a woman stopped us. See how that sits with him.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Put the hammers down. I won't ask twice. I never did learn how.

lines.speaker: ebbing
lines.line: Two dollars, Wade. Two dollars, and now this.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: Augustus Fenn. Editor, proprietor, and as of this morning the only one of the three still standing.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Ruth Caddell. I read your Lantern in Bitter Spring. Four dollars the acre.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: Then you're one of my eleven readers. The other ten use it to wrap fish, which is at least honest work.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Who sent them?

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: Nobody sends anybody in Port Linden, Mrs. Caddell. Things simply happen to people who print the wrong numbers. Walk with me.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: The new glass on the left is the Meridian and Western land office. They replace a window before anybody's had the chance to break it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: And the building with the iron shutters?

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: The Linden Exchange Bank. Syndicate money sleeps there. So does most of the town's, though the town sleeps worse.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: A lawyer named Lucius Pell signs for both. Nobody's ever seen him carry anything heavier than a pen. Nobody's needed to.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I'm looking for Eben Shale.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: Everybody is. Eben's the one man in Port Linden who is always somewhere else when it happens.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: What I need is paper. A deed, a ledger, a signature where it oughtn't to be. Opinions I have plenty of. They don't stop anybody.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: And what do I get?

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: A name in print. Yours, if you want it. Pell's, if you can earn it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Print it. Ruth Caddell, widow of Tom Caddell, express messenger. Let it get around who's asking.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: Brave or foolish. In my trade we set them in the same type.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Leave me out of it. Paper keeps a long memory, and I'd like mine short.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: A reader who values her privacy. You'll be lonely in this town.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: Pell's clerk, Lyle Hask, carries the books between the land office and the bank. Tonight he carries them to the Corinthian. He plays cards badly and often.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then I'd better play well.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Gilt mirrors over a sawdust floor. Port Linden can't decide if it's rich or only loud.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: I wouldn't take that chair. The last man in it left in his shirtsleeves, and it was a good shirt.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: And you're telling me out of kindness.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Out of interest. Delphine Arceneaux. Del, to people I've lost money to, which is a short list, and I keep it that way.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: The dealer is Abel Stroud. The one with ink on his cuffs is Lyle Hask. The old one is Mr. Merrow, who has folded every hand since the war.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: If you sit, watch Stroud's hands when he squares the deck. Not his face. His face has never done anything worth watching.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Why tell me?

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Because if Stroud's dealing to Hask, he's dealing against me. I owe more than I'd like, to people who'd like more than I owe.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I'll mind my own cards.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Everybody does, cher. That's how Stroud eats.

lines.speaker: stroud
lines.line: Quarter ante. Fifty cents before the draw, a dollar after. The house deals. The house always deals.

lines.speaker: merrow
lines.line: Sit down or go home, madam. I'm seventy-one. I haven't the time for both.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Mr. Stroud, put the deck down. Face up, and slow. Let's all see what lives on the bottom of it.

lines.speaker: stroud
lines.line: The lady's had a long evening. Somebody fetch her a sarsaparilla.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Turn it over, Abel. I'd love to be wrong. I've had so little practice.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Twice. You square the deck twice before Mr. Hask's big hands, Mr. Stroud. A man that tidy ought to be keeping books.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You deal like a man with a train to catch, Mr. Stroud.

lines.speaker: stroud
lines.line: Fast hands are a dealer's living, ma'am. Say it again and they'll be a dealer's argument.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: She has the wrong finger on it but the right man. The bottom card, Abel. Show the table.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Well, I won't let it go. Abel, you've dealt Lyle the bottom of the deck all night, and I am tired of paying for it.

lines.speaker: stroud
lines.line: Nobody calls the house a cheat in the house. Floyd!

lines.speaker: hask
lines.line: I keep books. I don't keep guns. Whatever Stroud did, he did it with his own hands.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: And whose money did his hands win?

lines.speaker: hask
lines.line: Mr. Quint's. Mr. Pell's. It's the same coat with two pockets.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Horace Quint holds my marker. Four hundred dollars, and Stroud has been adding to it all week, a dollar at a time.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Everybody takes back what he put in. It was never a game, so nobody won it.

lines.speaker: merrow
lines.line: Forty years at cards, and the first time anybody gave anything back. I may take up religion. Something moderate.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Stroud owes me for the evening. I'll collect it off the felt.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Practical. I admire that in a woman. I'd admire it less in a partner.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Quint will want his four hundred by Saturday. After that he'll want me, and not for my conversation.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've got a camp at Willow Bend. A drover who sings hymns badly and a boy who steals horses back. There's room.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Is that charity, Mrs. Caddell? I come out in hives.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It's work. You know money. I want to know where it's going, and where it's been.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Then I'll bring my own deck. Nobody touches it but me.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Go home, Mr. Hask. Tell Mr. Pell his clerk lost at cards. It'll be the first true line in his books.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Hask's books said Thornwood timber, paid in Exchange notes. Pine country and paper money. One of them's bound to burn.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: You'll want somebody who knows the camp. Which dogs bite and which ones just carry on about it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: What I'll want is you back at Willow Bend, helping Hap with the fence.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Hap said you'd say that. Then he said he wasn't chasing me, on account of his stitches.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Who runs the camp?

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Lew Tolliver. He says I owe twenty-two dollars for boots and board. The boots were two sizes big. I grew into one of 'em.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Go home, Billy.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Yes'm. Home's this way, as it happens. Through the timber. Past the camp.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Stay behind me. When I say run, you run, and you don't look back to see if I meant it.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: I'm awful good at running. It's most of what I'm good at.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: That's the flume up yonder. They float the logs down to the lake when there's water. There ain't been water since July.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Drought's hard on a timber camp.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Drought's hard on everybody but the men buying. Tolliver says that's only business. Tolliver says a lot of things, mostly loud.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Get down. That's him by the cook shack. The one in the city coat ain't from here.

lines.speaker: tolliver
lines.line: Pell's notes are paper. My men want silver. Paper don't spend in Thornwood.

lines.speaker: cobb
lines.line: Paper spends everywhere, Tolliver, once there's nobody left to refuse it. The Exchange holds the silver. Thursday night it holds a good deal of it.

lines.speaker: tolliver
lines.line: And if somebody was to walk in Thursday and take it off them?

lines.speaker: cobb
lines.line: Then Mr. Pell would be terribly surprised. He's arranged to be.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Arranged to be surprised. That's a lawyer's sentence if I ever heard one.

lines.speaker: tolliver
lines.line: Pruitt! I see you, boy! You owe me for boots!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Twenty-two dollars. For boots two sizes big, that's the dearest leather in the territory.

lines.speaker: tolliver
lines.line: Done. Take him, and his appetite with him. He eats like a mule.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: I don't eat like a mule. Mules eat better.

lines.speaker: cobb
lines.line: That woman was at the Corinthian. Mr. Pell will want to know where she goes. See that she doesn't get there.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: He owes you nothing. You had two summers of work out of him for one pair of boots.

lines.speaker: tolliver
lines.line: Then I'll take it out of you, lady. Boys!

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: You paid for me. Nobody ever paid for me. Except the boots, and I paid for those twice.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: They'd have dragged me back. You know that? By the collar, like a stray.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Don't make it into something. You're a hand now. Hands work.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Yes'm. What do I call you? Mrs. Caddell sounds like a schoolteacher.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Ruth will do. And Billy. Thursday night, the Exchange. You didn't hear any of it.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Hear any of what?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Here's what I've got. Call the rest the wages you never paid him.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Two watchmen. One old, one asleep. The back door's a Yale lock that thinks it's cleverer than it is.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: That city coat at Thornwood said Pell had arranged to be surprised.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Lawyers say all sorts of things. They charge by the word, so they say a great many.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Somebody let a boy and a woman with a gun hear exactly where the silver sleeps. That's not luck, Del. That's an invitation.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Then we're expected, and it would be rude not to come. Four hundred dollars, Ruth. Quint doesn't send a second letter. He sends a man.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: We go in. We take nothing I can't carry and can't explain.

lines.speaker: dodd
lines.line: I'm sixty-one years old and they pay me two dollars a week. You'll not find a hero in this coat.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I wasn't looking for one. Hold still. The knot's for your sake, so they'll know you never opened the door.

lines.speaker: dodd
lines.line: Who's there? I've a whistle, and I'm not afraid to blow it!

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: He's not afraid to blow it. Wonderful. Inside, Ruth, now. We've a minute less than we had.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: It's empty. Ruth, it's empty. Not a dime. Somebody swept it out like a church on a Monday.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Not empty. Look at this box. Quitclaim deeds. Willow Bend. The Ybarra well. Halvorsen's south section.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Arliss Doane signed this one on the twelfth. I stood at his grave on the tenth.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: There's a satchel by the door. Fifty dollars, maybe. It's bait, Ruth. It's practically wearing a bow.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Bait or not, it's money, and they've already decided what to call me.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: That's the spirit I was afraid of.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Leave it. Whoever left it there can explain it.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Fifty dollars on the floor of a bank and you step over it. I'll never understand you, and I'm going to enjoy trying.

lines.speaker: deputy
lines.line: Linden County! Come out of the Exchange with your hands where God can see them!

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: That's not the watchman. Those are deputies, and deputies don't come in ones.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: They were waiting. Not for a thief. For you. Somebody wanted Ruth Caddell standing in an empty vault.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then they've got their picture. And I've got their paper.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Paper burns, cher.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Not once it's printed. Fenn has a press and nothing left to lose.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Those deputies had wives and a county wage. They came because a lawyer told them where to stand.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Mr. Yale and I have an understanding. He makes the locks, and I make him look foolish.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Out the back and up the river road. Don't stop to argue with them. They've been told what to think.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Sun's up. Fenn will want these before the ink in his head dries.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: They used the drawing off the old Exhibition bills. I was nineteen. They've added the scar.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. We have a guest. He let himself in before I'd unlocked, which is remarkable in a man who isn't a burglar.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: Lucius Pell. Don't get up, Augustus, it's your chair. Mrs. Caddell, you look like your likeness, which is rare. Most people disappoint their posters.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: I read about you in the Lantern. Tom Caddell's widow, asking questions. I make a point of reading the Lantern. Someone should.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: Mr. Greer sold me your name for six dollars. I'd have paid twenty. I hope that doesn't hurt your feelings.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You put my face on a door.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: The county did. I described you. Accurately, I'd like to think. I'm told the reward is generous.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: For an empty vault.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: The vault held eleven thousand dollars on Thursday afternoon. The bank's books say so. Books, Mrs. Caddell, are what a court believes.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: You have papers that belong to my clients. Return them and the complaint is withdrawn. A clerical error. They happen.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Arliss Doane signed one of those papers two days after his funeral. Was that clerical?

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: Mr. Doane was a man of remarkable energy.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Take them.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: Sensible. You'll find sense is a cheaper habit than courage, and it keeps longer.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: I'll set the shipping news, then. Ships at least go somewhere.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I'll keep them. Your clients may apply to me, care of the Lantern.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: As you like. I never argue with people, Mrs. Caddell. I outlast them.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: Then I print tonight, and God look after my windows.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: There are two men across the street reading your poster very slowly. I don't believe it's the prose.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Back door?

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: Through the composing room. Mind the type cases. They've been through enough this week.

lines.speaker: breck
lines.line: Two hundred dollars standing in the street! Mrs. Caddell! Don't make me spoil the likeness.

lines.speaker: breck
lines.line: Fella at the bank says your paper's been pulled. Fella at the bank ain't paying me.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: There's a picture of you nailed up by the depot in Bitter Spring. They gave you a hard mouth.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I have a hard mouth.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Well. They spelled Caddell right. That's more than anybody ever did for Lindqvist.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Your price is higher than mine ever got. I've been worth less, and I've been worth a great deal more, but never in print.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: I could take it down. Nobody looks twice at a kid by the depot.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Do I get a poster? When I'm older?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: No poster, Billy. Not ever.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Tom used to say the company's real guns were the pens. I thought it was something messengers said to feel brave.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Supper's beans. I'm told that's a crime in Linden County too.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Withdrawn, the notice says. Nobody in the history of the world has believed a notice that says withdrawn.
